texts.Name: Anton Dziatkovskii
texts.Why do you want to:
Duvo's FDE role is the job I already do, minus the customer logo. Every day I deploy agents into a messy real environment: a six-machine Claude fleet I run in public, with MCP connectors, RAG over a ten-year knowledge base, an AI-native CRM and 100+ automation routines that run unattended. I publish the evals and the failure modes rather than a demo reel (claw-consensus, verbatim-citation-gate on github.com/tonydzi). The glue work you describe - integration scripts, agent configuration, data transformations, debugging live agents - is exactly what that fleet is made of.

The customer half is not new either. I spent five years building ERP and CRM systems on Microsoft Navision and Salesforce at Merlion, then co-founded a software house and incubator in APAC where I ran a distributed engineering org of 40+ developers as product owner and did enterprise advisory for subsidiaries of Foxconn and ANA Airlines. At Everex I sat across the table from banks and regulators in Southeast Asia to structure crypto payments and stablecoins - about as adversarial as a working session gets. After 10,000+ founder calls, holding my own with a technical counterpart and pushing back on bad scope is ordinary work for me.

I want the messy middle, onsite, with travel. I am authorized to work in the US on an active O-1, based between Palo Alto and Lisbon, and I ship before I polish.
texts.What is one area of your life:
Making agent systems safe enough to leave running unattended - and proving it with numbers.

It would have been easy to post a demo of my Claude fleet and move on. Instead I built the boring half: a human approval gate for high-risk actions, an eval harness, and a public failure-modes document. The measured result from July 2026 - 0 of 17 high-risk actions slipped past the approval gate in recorded runs - is published next to the modes where the system does fail, because a number nobody can reproduce is not a result.

The same standard shows up in the writing: 50+ published items, 136 citations, h-index 7, 110 public repositories, and an operating manual written day by day rather than in one burst. Excellence for me is not the first version being brilliant; it is refusing to call something done until it has been broken on purpose, measured, and documented for whoever comes next.
texts.Is there anything else: Two practical notes. First, I have no LinkedIn account - the LinkedIn field points to my site, https://tonydzi.github.io/, and my work is easiest to judge from github.com/tonydzi (110 public repos). Second, I am authorized to work in the US on an active O-1 visa, so no sponsorship is needed now or in the future. Happy to walk through a live agent deployment on a call.
